text: Rob Copeland investigates Ray Dalio and the internal culture of Bridgewater Associates, drawing on interviews with people inside and around the investment firm. The account examines the gap between Dalio's public management philosophy and employees' experiences of surveillance, conflict, and pressure. It follows the people drawn into Bridgewater's orbit and questions the assumption that extraordinary financial success necessarily makes its architects reliable guides to human behavior.
author: Rob Copeland
